name: Quadratics
description: Factorise, solve and sketch quadratics, find the price that maximises revenue, then work with surds, algebraic fractions, cubics and circles.

requires.why: Expands brackets with area models and takes out common factors before factorising quadratics.
Solves linear equations step by step before applying the quadratic formula and discriminant.
Uses square roots and index laws in the quadratic formula.
Solves linear inequalities such as 64 − 4c > 0 to find which constants give two roots.
Sketches parabolas and reads roots and turning points from graphs of functions.
Solves quadratic inequalities and rearranges formulae using the inequality rules.
Substitutes a line into a curve, as simultaneous equations with one linear and one quadratic do.
Uses prime factors and highest common factors to simplify surds and cancel fractions.

lessonNames.l2-product-and-sum: Two numbers from a product and a sum
lessonNames.l3-leading-coefficient: When the square term has a coefficient
lessonNames.l5-product-of-zero: Why a product of zero helps
lessonNames.l11-meeting-the-axis: Where the curve meets the axis
lessonNames.l16-adding-and-solving: Adding fractions and solving with them
lessonNames.l19-line-meets-curve: Where a line meets a curve

lessonObjectives.l1-two-brackets: Expand $(x + a)(x + b)$ with an area model and spot where each term comes from.
lessonObjectives.l2-product-and-sum: Factorise $x^2 + bx + c$ by finding the pair with the right product and sum.
lessonObjectives.l3-leading-coefficient: Factorise $ax^2 + bx + c$ by splitting the middle term.
lessonObjectives.l4-difference-of-squares: Recognise and factorise $a^2 - b^2$ on sight.
lessonObjectives.l5-product-of-zero: Solve a factorised quadratic by setting each bracket to zero.
lessonObjectives.l6-completing-the-square: Rewrite a quadratic as a square plus a constant using a square diagram.
lessonObjectives.l7-the-formula: Derive the quadratic formula by completing the square, then use it.
lessonObjectives.l8-how-many-solutions: Use the discriminant to count real roots before solving.
lessonObjectives.l9-shape-of-a-square: Sketch $y = x^2$ and its relatives and read their line of symmetry.
lessonObjectives.l10-turning-point: Read the vertex of a parabola from its completed square form.
lessonObjectives.l11-meeting-the-axis: Connect roots, intercepts and the discriminant on a sketch.
lessonObjectives.l12-above-or-below: Solve a quadratic inequality from a sketch of the parabola.
lessonObjectives.l13-best-price: Model revenue as a quadratic in price and find the price that maximises it.
lessonObjectives.l14-roots-that-stay: Simplify surds, add and multiply them, and rationalise a denominator.
lessonObjectives.l15-fractions-with-letters: Simplify, multiply and divide algebraic fractions by factorising and cancelling common factors.
lessonObjectives.l16-adding-and-solving: Add and subtract algebraic fractions over a common denominator, and solve equations that contain them.
lessonObjectives.l17-dividing-polynomials: Divide a polynomial by a linear factor, and use the factor theorem to factorise a cubic.
lessonObjectives.l18-circles-on-a-grid: Find the distance between two points, and write and read the equation of a circle.
lessonObjectives.l19-line-meets-curve: Find where a line meets a parabola or a circle, and use the discriminant to tell crossing from touching from missing.
